summary.name: MetaGPT
summary.one_liner: MetaGPT is an arXiv research paper introducing a meta-programming framework that uses LLM-based agents with assigned roles and human-style standardized workflows to collaborate on complex tasks such as software engineering.
use_cases: Understanding role-based agent workflows for software engineering
Reducing errors from chained LLM calls
Reference for automated problem solving with agent teams
summary.what_it_does: The paper introduces MetaGPT, a framework that encodes Standardized Operating Procedures into prompt sequences so LLM agents follow human-like workflows. It uses an assembly line paradigm to assign diverse roles to agents and break complex tasks into subtasks. The authors intend agents to verify intermediate results to reduce cascading errors. The abstract reports that on collaborative software engineering benchmarks, MetaGPT generates more coherent solutions than previous chat-based multi-agent systems. The page is the arXiv abstract listing (v1 submitted August 2023, latest revision November 2024) and links to a project repository on GitHub.
notable: Encodes human Standardized Operating Procedures (SOPs) into LLM prompt sequences
Assembly line paradigm assigning distinct roles to agents
Aims to reduce cascading hallucinations from naively chained LLMs
caveats: Page is an arXiv abstract; platform and licensing details are not stated on this page
Benchmark claims are reported only as stated in the abstract
